description: Unify new Plaid onboarding around transactions plus optional liabilities, then add a dedicated update-mode path for legacy Items that need liability consent later without forcing delete-and-relink behavior.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 14 should land first so institution lifecycle semantics are stable before adding more Item-management surface area.

principles: Default new-item onboarding should succeed even when liability consent is not granted
Liabilities should be requested opportunistically, not required for every institution
Existing Items need a first-class upgrade path instead of delete-and-relink workarounds
Login repair and permission upgrade must be treated as separate actions
Item-level capability state should be persisted rather than inferred forever from sparse sync results

techStack.plaid: Link token creation, optional products, and update-mode product/consent expansion
techStack.testing: node:test integration tests for token creation behavior, item status tracking, and sync visibility

userStories.title: Default new links request liabilities opportunistically
acceptanceCriteria: Default new-item link token requests transactions as the required product
Default new-item link token also requests liabilities as an optional product
Ordinary bank onboarding can still succeed when liability consent is not granted
The split onboarding assumption that liabilities require a separate institution flow is removed
userStories.testStrategy: Route-level integration test confirming default link token includes optional liabilities instead of required liabilities.

userStories.title: Legacy items can upgrade to liability consent
acceptanceCriteria: A dedicated update-mode route exists for enabling liabilities on an existing Item
Permission upgrade is distinct from login repair in both routing and UI
OAuth resume and link session tracking continue to work for the upgrade flow
Users are not required to delete and relink an institution just to enable liabilities
userStories.testStrategy: Integration tests for token-creation route shape plus manual validation on an OAuth institution that previously lacked liability consent.

userStories.title: Persist item-level liability access state
acceptanceCriteria: Items track whether liability access is enabled, missing, unsupported, or still unknown
Legacy transactions-only items can be identified without relying entirely on sync heuristics
Settings uses persisted item state to decide when to show Enable liabilities
Non-fatal liability-consent issues do not mark the whole Item as broken
userStories.testStrategy: Migration/integration tests for item state persistence plus sync tests for non-fatal consent-required behavior.

userStories.title: Clarify liability upgrade action in Settings
acceptanceCriteria: Settings shows an explicit Enable liabilities action when an Item is upgradeable
Fix login remains focused on ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED / reauth behavior
Items already confirmed liability-enabled do not keep showing the upgrade CTA
UI copy makes clear that liability access is additive and institution-dependent
userStories.testStrategy: Manual Settings verification and route smoke tests.

high: Plaid update-mode product-consent mechanics are the most failure-prone part of this feature and must be confirmed before implementation
medium: Optional liabilities on default links may still produce institution-specific OAuth edge cases
Persisted capability state can drift if not updated consistently during link, sync, and upgrade flows
low: Some institutions may never expose liabilities even after consent, which the UI can explain without treating as an error

preFlightChecklist: Confirm the exact Plaid request shape for additional liability consent in update mode before implementation
Decide the final item-level liability_access_status state machine
Confirm how legacy transactions-only Items are initialized into the new state model
Verify at least one real institution can be used for end-to-end upgrade validation
